model.title: Veterans’ Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Veterans' Compensation Cost-of-Living Adjustment Act of 2026

This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to increase the amounts payable for wartime disability compensation, additional compensation for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children. Specifically, the VA must increase the amounts by the same percentage as the cost-of-living increase in benefits for Social Security recipients that is effective on December 1, 2026. The act requires the VA to publish the amounts payable, as increased, in the Federal Register.
The VA is authorized to make a similar adjustment to the rates of disability compensation payable to persons who have not received compensation for service-connected disability or death.

This bill requires the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) to raise several benefit payments for veterans and their families. The payments covered are wartime disability compensation, extra compensation for dependents, the clothing allowance for certain disabled veterans, and dependency and indemnity compensation for surviving spouses and children.

The increase is set by the same percentage as the cost-of-living increase for Social Security recipients that takes effect on December 1, 2026. In other words, the veterans' payments rise by that same percentage.
The VA must publish the new, higher payment amounts in the Federal Register, the official government publication where such notices appear.
The VA is also allowed, though not required, to make a similar adjustment to disability compensation rates for people who have not received compensation for a service-connected disability or death.
